messages:
customer_acme: Hey @sara_support — we're hitting 415 when trying to stream rerank results. We updated our client to use SSE and are POSTing to /v1/rerank with Accept: text/event-stream and Content-Type: text/event-stream. Server responds with 415 and body: {"error":"unsupported content type for rerank: text/event-stream"}. Example curl we used:

```
  curl -N \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n    -H "Content-Type: text/event-stream" \n    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n    -d '{"query":"which of these is about billing?","candidates":["billing faq","api auth","sso"]}'
```

Is streaming officially supported for /v1/rerank? We're trying to stream because the candidate set is large and we want progressive UI updates.

sara_support: Thanks for the report — sorry for the friction. Short answer: the rerank endpoint does NOT support streaming responses. It expects a synchronous JSON request and returns a JSON payload of scores. Content-Type should be application/json and Accept: application/json. Streaming (SSE) is only available for generation endpoints.

Couple of helpful things to check: the server error you pasted looks right for the current behavior — the runtime rejects text/event-stream on rerank routes. Can you paste the full request body you used (sanitized token)? Also which model variant exactly (you mentioned rerank-large-1)?

customer_acme: Model: rerank-large-1. Body was exactly the curl above. We also saw a 401 once when using an expired token, but 415 is consistent when we try SSE. Our candidate set is ~2k items, we were hoping to stream progressive scores rather than wait ~6s for the whole pass.

sara_support: Two notes: 1) token 401 is expected if it expired — use a fresh token for reproducible repros. 2) rerank has a candidate limit (we enforce a hard cap, currently 1024 candidates per request) — sending 2k will hit a validation error on the server. If you need to score >1024 candidates, you'll need to batch on the client.

mike_eng: tagging eng-runtime — can you share the request id/debug id shown in the response? Also post the exact response body for both the 415 and the validation error (if you hit the candidate cap). The code path for rerank is single-shot (no streaming). If you want a streaming-like UX, you can do progressive batching from the client: send smaller candidate chunks and render partial sorted results as they return.

customer_acme: Response body (for 415): {"error":"unsupported content type for rerank: text/event-stream","debug_id":"dbg_7f9a2"}
Response body (when we split into 2 requests of ~1k each) is OK but final latency is higher overall. We'd really prefer server streaming otherwise we'd have to write a lot of client-side glue.

jamie_sre: I reproduced locally with the same headers. Confirmed: server handler returns HTTP/415 when Content-Type is text/event-stream. Stack trace points to a content-negotiation check in rerank handler. Filing a follow-up with eng-runtime to consider returning a clearer error message and to document the non-streaming behavior in the rerank API docs.

mike_eng: For transparency — streaming for rerank is non-trivial because the rerank scoring pipeline expects the full candidate set to build internal caches and optimize scoring kernels (KV reuse, quantization paths). Streaming would change how we batch and could degrade scoring consistency. It's not on the short-term roadmap.

sara_support: Practical next steps for you:
- Change Content-Type to application/json and Accept to application/json. Use the standard rerank request body: {"query":"...","candidates":[...]}
- If you need progressive UI, implement client-side chunking (e.g., 250-500 candidates per request) and merge results client-side.
- If you see unexpected identical scores or score saturation, include the model name + debug_id. We can check for numeric underflow/quantization artifacts.

customer_acme: Ok will try batching. One more thing — when we saw identical scores for different candidates, we got worried it's a bug in rerank. Any quick guidance on what causes that?

mike_eng: Identical scores can come from three places: 1) exact tie given model scoring (rare but possible), 2) quantization/coarse scoring bins for small differences (more likely on quantized variants), 3) input truncation causing candidates to be identical after tokenization. Best repro steps: supply two candidates that you think should differ, give us debug_id, and we'll run the internal eval. Also include whether you're on a quantized model variant.

customer_acme: We're on rerank-large-1-8bit (quantized). I'll repro with a tiny candidate pair and share debug_id.

sara_support: Thanks — I'll keep ticket CS-4821 updated. If you hit auth/billing errors again (401/402), paste the full response and the token creation time. For the streaming 415 path, we'll add a small note to docs to avoid confusion.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: deploy finished for docs/rerank-content-type-fix (commit 8f3a2b) — PR updates note that rerank endpoints are non-streaming and clarify candidate limits.

sara_support: Closing loop here: temporary workaround = client-side chunking. Eng has noted potential doc/err improvements. If you want, we can schedule a short sync to review UX tradeoffs.

customer_acme: That works, thanks everyone. Will reopen if we find a repro for identical scores. :thumbsup:
